title: ABA Model Rules of Professional Conduct: Rules 1.6, 1.8(b) and 1.9(c) (Confidentiality and No-Adverse-Use)
author: American Bar Association · House of Delegates

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source supplies generally applicable duties on confidentiality, information security, client consent and professional independence that are relevant to AI governance, but it does not address AI capability, task selection, verification, human–AI work allocation or operating-model redesign. It therefore neither accepts nor rejects the cluster’s principal proposition.
qs: (c)  A lawyer shall make reasonable efforts to prevent the inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of, or unauthorized access to, information relating to the representation of a client.

(f)  A lawyer shall not accept compensation for representing a client from one other than the client unless:  (1)  the client gives informed consent;  (2)  there is no interference with the lawyer's independence of professional judgment or with the client-lawyer relationship; and  (3)  information relating to representation of a client is protected as required by Rule 1.6.

kp.k: Confidentiality prohibits disclosure subject to specified authorizations
kp.d: Model Rule 1.6(a) prohibits revealing information relating to a client's representation unless the client gives informed consent, disclosure is impliedly authorized to carry out the representation, or paragraph (b) permits disclosure. The document states professional rules rather than findings or predictions about AI.
qs: A lawyer shall not reveal information relating to the representation of a client
the disclosure is impliedly authorized in order to carry out the representation

kp.k: Disclosure exceptions are permissive and limited by necessity
kp.d: Rule 1.6(b) permits disclosure only to the extent the lawyer reasonably believes necessary. Its exceptions cover preventing reasonably certain death or substantial bodily harm; preventing specified client crime or fraud involving the lawyer's services; preventing, mitigating or rectifying specified financial or property injury from such conduct; obtaining advice on compliance with the Rules; specified lawyer claims, defenses and responses to allegations; compliance with other law or court orders; and qualified conflict checks.
qs: to the extent the lawyer reasonably believes necessary
to prevent reasonably certain death or substantial bodily harm
to comply with other law or a court order

kp.k: Conflict-check disclosures must preserve privilege and avoid prejudice
kp.d: Rule 1.6(b)(7) permits disclosures to detect and resolve conflicts arising from a lawyer's employment change or changes in firm composition or ownership, but only when disclosure would neither compromise attorney-client privilege nor otherwise prejudice the client.
qs: to detect and resolve conflicts of interest arising from the lawyer’s change of employment
would not compromise the attorney-client privilege or otherwise prejudice the client

kp.k: Reasonable safeguards must prevent disclosure and unauthorized access
kp.d: Rule 1.6(c) requires reasonable efforts to prevent inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of representation-related information and unauthorized access to that information. The supplied text specifies no particular technology or AI-specific safeguarding procedure.
qs: A lawyer shall make reasonable efforts to prevent the inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure of
or unauthorized access to, information relating to the representation of a client.

kp.k: Client information cannot be used against current clients
kp.d: Rule 1.8(b) separately prohibits using representation-related information to a current client's disadvantage unless the client gives informed consent, except as permitted or required by the Rules. This restriction concerns use of information, not merely its disclosure.
qs: to the disadvantage of the client unless the client gives informed consent
except as permitted or required by these Rules.

kp.k: Third-party payment preserves confidentiality and professional independence
kp.d: Rule 1.8(f) permits compensation from someone other than the client only with the client's informed consent, no interference with professional judgment or the client-lawyer relationship, and protection of representation-related information as required by Rule 1.6.
qs: the client gives informed consent
there is no interference with the lawyer's independence of professional judgment
information relating to representation of a client is protected as required by Rule 1.6.

kp.k: Current-client prohibitions extend across associated firm lawyers
kp.d: Rule 1.8(k) applies the prohibitions in paragraphs (a) through (i) to all lawyers associated in a firm when a prohibition applies to any one of them. This includes paragraph (b)'s restriction on disadvantageous use of client information.
qs: a prohibition in the foregoing paragraphs (a) through (i)
shall apply to all of them.

kp.k: Former-client duties distinguish adverse use from revelation
kp.d: Rule 1.9(c) covers clients formerly represented by the lawyer or the lawyer's present or former firm. It prohibits disadvantageous use of representation-related information except as the Rules permit or require for a client, or when the information has become generally known. Revelation is separately prohibited except as the Rules permit or require for a client; the revelation provision contains no generally-known exception.
qs: or whose present or former firm has formerly represented a client in a matter
or when the information has become generally known
reveal information relating to the representation except as these Rules would permit or require

kp.k: Former-client conflicts constrain subsequent adverse representations
kp.d: Rule 1.9(a) bars subsequent representation in the same or a substantially related matter where interests are materially adverse to a former client, absent that client's informed consent confirmed in writing. Paragraph (b) similarly restricts knowingly undertaking such representation involving a former firm's client when the lawyer acquired protected information material to the matter, subject to the same consent requirement.
qs: in the same or a substantially related matter
unless the former client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
information protected by Rules 1.6 and 1.9(c) that is material to the matter

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The source makes no concrete claims or predictions about AI changing legal services.
pts.d: The ABA provisions prescribe confidentiality and restrictions on adverse use of current and former clients' information. They do not mention AI or describe technological changes to legal work, staffing, or markets. Applying these provisions to AI would require analysis beyond the source's express statements.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: No evidence is offered for an AI-related claim.
pts.d: The document is normative authority—the text of ABA Model Rules—not an empirical study or forecast. It supplies no AI data, benchmarks, cases, or experience. These are Model Rules, not an identified jurisdiction's adopted rules.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: No AI-related timeframe or adoption conditions are stated.
pts.d: The provisions instead specify conditions governing disclosure and use of client information: informed consent, authorization, enumerated exceptions, and reasonable efforts to prevent unauthorized disclosure or access. Former-client duties continue after representation. Rule 1.9(c)(1)'s generally-known exception concerns adverse use; paragraph (c)(2) does not state that exception for disclosure. These are qualifications to professional duties, not predictions about AI.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The provisions address lawyers and protect current and former clients; no AI-specific affected group is identified.
pts.d: Lawyers bear confidentiality and no-adverse-use duties. Rule 1.8(k) extends the prohibitions in paragraphs (a) through (i), including paragraph (b), to associated lawyers in a firm. Rule 1.9(c) covers information from representation by the lawyer or the lawyer's present or former firm. The source does not attribute any AI-driven effects to these groups.
